questions.Q1: You observe high cross-lingual representational similarity between English and a target language, but an intervention transfers inconsistently at the behavioural level. How would you interpret this result, and what would you test next?
questions.Q2: You are evaluating an LLM on a benchmark translated from English into several languages. What would make you question whether performance differences reflect model capability rather than translation or dataset artifacts?
questions.Q3: A multilingual model performs substantially worse in a low-resource language. How would you investigate whether tokenization is a major cause rather than merely a correlated explanation?
questions.Q4: You need to evaluate open-ended responses from a multilingual LLM, but there is no single correct reference answer. How would you choose an evaluation method, and what limitations would you report?
questions.Q5: Your results change noticeably across model families, layers, prompts or random seeds. How would you decide whether you have found a meaningful effect or an unstable experimental artifact?
questions.Q6: You inherit a multilingual LLM experiment repository whose reported results you cannot reproduce. What would you inspect first, and how would you determine where the discrepancy comes from?
questions.Q7: A reviewer argues that your experiment shows only a correlation between an internal representation and model behaviour, not a causal relationship. How would you respond or redesign the experiment?
questions.Q8: One language produces a result in the opposite direction from the others, even though the implementation checks pass. How would you investigate and report that result?
